learning_outcomes.text: Acquire knowledge about the basic principles of separation and purification processes in biological systems.
Ability to analyze problems related to bioseparation processes and generate solutions.
Equip students with the ability to work effectively in interdisciplinary teams.
Make students aware of the need to continuously update themselves by following developments in science and technology.
Equip students with the ability to communicate effectively in written and oral form.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to separation processes in bioprocesses
Pre-treatment processes (sedimentation, foam separation, flocculation, coagulation, precipitation)
bibliography: R. G. Harrison, P. Todd, S. R. Rudge, D. P. Petrides, “Bioseparations Science and Engineering”, Oxford University Press, 2006.

C. J. Geankoplis, “Transport Processes and Separation Process (Includes Unit Operations)”, Prentice Hall, 4th Edition, 2003.
